section: Introduction
focus: Surveys and systematic reviews of large language models in literature review, evidence synthesis and biomedical data extraction (accuracy, citation fidelity and automation levels reported), up to 2026-11.
context: Hook: Curated knowledge bases in human genetics (OMIM, ClinVar, the Human Phenotype Ontology annotations, ClinGen gene-disease validity) are written by experts who read papers and record, entry by entry, what each paper showed; curation is slow relative to the literature, and language models can now read the papers. Many system designs turn documents into structured, cited text (long-context reading, retrieval augmentation, extraction into a graph or table, agents that choose what to read, draft-then-verify, optimised prompts), but each was evaluated on a different task, model, retrieval stack and scoring, so their results cannot be compared.. Gap: No controlled comparison holds the model, the sources, the guards and the scoring fixed on the curator's own task: writing an entry from exactly the papers the curators cited and scoring what the draft says about each paper against what the curators wrote about it. Scoped strictly to what the log evaluates: one model family; OMIM phenotype entries with 2-12 references (plus small exploratory tiers); open-access text only (19% of cited papers readable in full); a variant-centred per-paper reference. Three open questions: how much the generation strategy matters under one control; whether access to the source or the strategy limits agreement with curator-written text; and which errors a claim-level audit against the cited source catches and which it cannot see. The paper is an evaluation and benchmark contribution, not a new method and not a clinical tool.

section: Related Work: 2.1 Language models for literature curation in genetics and biology
focus: benchmarking LLM gene-disease-phenotype extraction full-text human genetics literature
context: Mission: Find work published up to 2026-11 that generates or extracts curated genetics or biology knowledge from papers and scores it against expert curation. For the four closest neighbours named in notes.md (FlyAOC: memorisation, pipeline and agent harnesses against FlyBase curators; GEN-KnowRD: generated rare-disease profiles against curated reports; WikiCrow: gene articles against Wikipedia; Groza et al. 2026: model memory of rare-disease genes and phenotypes) establish exactly what is held fixed, what the reference is and whether sources are searched or given. Do not look for new systems to beat.. Hypothesis: Prior curation work either lets the system search a corpus for its sources (confounding retrieval with writing), measures memory alone, compares models rather than generation strategies, or scores against something other than what curators wrote about each cited paper; none manipulates access to the source text within the same papers.

section: Related Work: 2.2 Intermediate representations versus long-context reading
focus: knowledge graph extraction before generation versus full-document reading evaluation
context: Mission: Identify controlled comparisons, published up to 2026-11, in which the backbone model is held fixed while the reading or intermediate representation varies; record their task (question answering, query-focused summarisation, literature QA), input sizes, and whether released pipelines were run with a model other than their default. section: Related Work: 2.3 Memory, verification and contamination
focus: time-based contamination analysis training cutoff newly created test items
context: Mission: Establish, up to 2026-11, what draft-then-verify methods are designed to do (remove or correct unsupported content versus add missing content) and on which tasks they were evaluated; and which contamination checks rely on creation dates or post-cut-off test items, since curated knowledge bases are public.. Hypothesis: Verify-after-recall methods are evaluated on short-form QA or biographies and correct or delete content rather than recover what the sources state; contamination checks are rarely applied to knowledge-base writing, where the reference itself is public and older entries are better known.

section: 1. Introduction - 1. Introduction
focus: Piwowar (The state of OA: a large-scale analysis of the prevalence and impact of Open Access articles)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Structure for the literature agent, so that the Introduction and the results agree; literature comes from intro_related_work_plan. About 1.2 pages including fig_overview. P1 hook: curated knowledge bases are written entry by entry from papers; OMIM as the example (about 7,000 phenotype entries with a known molecular basis, idea.md 'Problem'); the design space for turning documents into cited, structured text (long-context reading, retrieval, graph or table intermediates, agents, draft-then-verify, optimised prompts), each with one citation. P2 gap: these designs were evaluated on different tasks, models, retrieval stacks and scoring; controlled comparisons exist for question answering and summarisation, not for the curator's task; state the three questions of idea.md 'Problem' verbatim in substance. P3 what we do: a benchmark in which the strategy is the only variable (fig_overview): 100 entries with 2-12 references, 515 papers of which 19% are readable in full (log Sec. 1.1); paradigms, a control and add-ons each tested against its parent (never 'nine strategies'); the primary endpoint 'OMIM facts conveyed' defined in one sentence as coverage of facts in OMIM's allelic-variant descriptions as deposited in ClinVar, split once without sight of any draft (notes.md 'Words to use'); make explicit that each strategy writes a whole entry but only what it says about each cited paper is scored against this variant-centred text. P4 four findings, each a bold lead sentence plus one or two numbers, mirroring Sections 4.1-4.5: (i) access bounds agreement (79.8% vs 36.1% within the same papers; 91.0-94.4% of stated vs under 7% of not-stated facts); (ii) changing the design did not beat direct reading in this regime, our case-table implementation falls behind where full text is readable, and released pipelines conveyed fewer facts at the settings tested (exploratory); (iii) reading the supplied text more completely recovers a few points (completeness pass +2.6 points on 38 held-out entries), far below what full text adds; (iv) the audit's blind spots (added citations, omissions; fidelity, not correctness). Acknowledge once that the direction of (i) is expected, since curators wrote from full papers; the contribution is its controlled size and what remains within reach. P5 contributions, at most four (compress idea.md 'Contributions' 1-7): benchmark and harness from public sources with fixed fact lists, claim-level audit and per-entry release; controlled comparison with completion as an outcome, run-to-run variation, a matched ablation, negative results for memory-first strategies and two add-ons, and released pipelines as reference points; the access findings plus a measured gain from reading better; the audit's coverage and measurement lessons. Then one scope sentence: one model family, no human validation, the curators' reference list is given to every strategy, drafts are for expert review and not clinical guidance.

section: 3. Benchmark and Strategies - 3.1 Task, entries and reference
focus: research paper or technical report introducing the 'NCBI Gene' database (source of the mim2gene mapping)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Formal setup exactly as idea.md 'Formal setup': entry e = (h, R), header h (number, title, alternative titles), references R = {d_1..d_n}, access level a(d) in {full text, abstract, title} set by open access; a strategy S maps (h, R) to a draft D (paragraphs citing non-empty subsets of R; sets of genes, inheritance modes, ontology terms, variants). The causal gene is withheld because naming it is part of the curator's task. Entries (log Sec. 1.1): 100 OMIM phenotype entries at random with a fixed seed, 20 from each of five entry-number bands that track creation date; eligibility (2-12 references, causal gene in the gene map, at least five phenotype annotations, at least one curator paragraph in scope) selects well-annotated, molecularly characterised entries. 515 papers: 96 (19%) readable in full through PubMed Central or Europe PMC, 345 abstract only, 74 title only; supplements not retrieved. Reference (log Sec. 1.1; wording from notes.md): curator-written per-paper text = OMIM's allelic-variant descriptions as deposited by OMIM in ClinVar, variant-centred prose from OMIM's gene entries; 476 paragraphs in scope; split once into 6,652 fixed facts without sight of any draft. The narrative sections of phenotype entries are not public and are not compared. Clinical synopsis reference = HPO disease annotations, 2,311, of which 1,835 are the HPO team's own curation and 476 taken from OMIM (never 'OMIM's synopsis'). Causal gene from OMIM's gene map via MedGen and mim2gene; inheritance from HPO and MedGen modes as coarse classes that must be equal as sets; 427 in-scope OMIM-submitted ClinVar variant records. Other entry sets in one sentence, pointing to an Appendix A table: 40-entry ablation set, 30-entry replicate set, held-out entries for the reading-better arms, entries created June-November 2026, and the small second-round sets (log Sec. 1.1, 5, 10, 14, 15).

section: 3. Benchmark and Strategies - 3.2 Strategies
focus: Zhang (Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Present as three paradigms, one control and three add-ons each tested against its parent (log Sec. 1.3 table; notes.md 'Venue and positioning'); full table in Appendix B. Read and write: direct reading (all papers in one prompt; baseline) and the agentic curator (read and search tools over a folder of the papers; a verbatim quote for every paragraph). Extract, then write: evidence graph (quote-backed findings per paper joined into a graph; findings whose quote is not in the paper are discarded; the writer sees only the graph; synopsis terms by rule) and case table first (one record per reported patient or family per paper, pooled; synopsis terms and inheritance by rule; the writer sees only the table). Memory first: recall, then verify (memory draft audited against the papers; the rewriter keeps, restates, corrects or deletes and may not add content from the papers). Control: memory only (no papers; audited, not repaired). Say 'our extract-then-write implementations' wherever a result may depend on implementation choices. Add-ons in one sentence each: second-hand evidence on direct reading (passages from later open-access papers describing a paper not readable in full, marked as second-hand); reconciled case database on case table first (propose, verify, apply merges of the same patient, family or variant); learned curation guide on direct reading (rules from two reflection rounds on 27 training entries). Reading better (evaluated in Section 4.3; log Sec. 15): checklist (direct reading with a curator checklist of what a curator records about each paper), completeness pass (per paper, a check lists findings the paper states that the draft omits, each with a quote verified in the paper, then one revision adding only those), three-draft merge (three direct-reading drafts merged keeping every distinct statement), and checklist + completeness pass. Chosen from a review of ten approaches by where direct reading loses facts (idea.md 'Core idea'). Guards for every strategy (log Sec. 1.3): ontology identifiers chosen only from ontology-search candidates; gene symbols normalised against HGNC; recalled entry cross-reference numbers removed; every paragraph must cite a supplied paper. Model (log Sec. 1.2): Claude Opus 5.5 for writing, extraction, audit and judging, through a command-line interface in headless mode with schema-constrained output; no temperature or seed; reasoning effort high for writers, medium for per-paper extraction, audit and judging; no web access; replies cached so each call is made once. A reply 'stopped by the model's safety filter' comes back empty, is recorded and never retried with a changed prompt; the reasons are not visible. Released systems are introduced where they are evaluated (Section 4.4), not here.

section: 3. Benchmark and Strategies - 3.3 Audit, scoring and statistics
focus: Verspoor (A categorization approach to automated ontological function annotation)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Completion (idea.md 'Formal setup'; log Sec. 1.4): S completes e when its draft exists and no per-paper call failed; a stopped reply costs a one-call strategy the whole entry and a per-paper strategy one paper, so comparisons use only entries every compared strategy completed, completion is reported as an outcome, and a sensitivity analysis counts a missing draft as zero. Audit (log Sec. 1.4): paragraphs split into atomic claims c attributed to cited papers R(c); each cited paper gives a verdict v(c, d) in {supported, partly supported, unsupported, contradicted} with a quote; a 'supported' verdict whose quote is not verbatim in the paper is downgraded; the claim takes the best verdict over R(c) (state this here: Section 4.5 shows it hides over-citation); flagged claims get one repair round. Words (notes.md): 'judged supported'; unsupported is not wrong; report unsupported and contradicted separately. Primary endpoint with one displayed equation: coverage(D) = (#present + 1/2 #partly present) / #facts judged over the fixed list Phi(g) of each in-scope curator paragraph, marked in what D says about the paragraph's papers; OMIM facts conveyed = mean over entries. Why fixed lists (idea.md 'Design rationale'): splitting afresh adapts the split to the draft and changes denominators. Availability judgement (log Sec. 2.10a, 3): every fixed fact carries a stored judgement of whether the text available for its paper states, partly states or does not state it ('stated' needs a verified quote); a property of the supplied text, the same for every strategy, and a model judgement. Secondary measures in two sentences (log Sec. 1.4): HPO terms by precision, recall and F1 (exact; hierarchical, with ancestors; semantic, best Lin similarity with information content from the annotations); allelic variants by recall and precision (normalised protein or nucleotide change, a model judge for names that do not normalise; not validated against reference sequences; precision counts a variant OMIM does not list as a miss even if the paper reports it); causal-gene F1; inheritance agreement; predicting nothing where the reference is non-empty scores zero. Statistics (log Sec. 1.4, 2.3a, 4.2): paired differences from direct reading, means over entries, bootstrap 95% interval over entries (10,000 resamples), better/worse/tied, exact two-sided sign test with ties dropped, Holm adjustment across the eight secondary headline measures within a strategy; the primary endpoint is not adjusted. Replicate noise (30 entries, three replicates) is a yardstick of how much a difference moves on repetition, not a test (notes.md). Aggregation convention stated once: levels are means over entries unless marked pooled.

section: 4. Experiments - 4.2 Strategies under one control
focus: White (LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Limited LLM Benchmark)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Table 1 (log Sec. 2.2 and 2.3; 93 of 100 entries completed by all six strategies; completion table in Appendix C). Rows grouped by paradigm, control last. Columns: OMIM facts conveyed; paired difference (95% CI) and better/worse/tied; claims judged supported; HPO F1 exact; variants recovered; variant precision (with n where below 93); causal-gene F1; generation list price per entry. Values: direct reading 49.1 / - / 96.1 / 35.9 / 66.5 / 88.7 (82) / 97.5 / $0.26; agentic curator 48.4 / -0.6 (-1.3, +0.0) 31/42/20 / 96.4 / 35.6 / 65.9 / 87.9 (82) / 97.5 / $0.28; evidence graph 48.6 / -0.5 (-1.5, +0.5) 33/45/15 / 96.5 / 34.6 / 65.9 / 76.9 (87) / 98.2 / $0.56; case table first 47.2 / -1.9 (-3.1, -0.8) 31/48/14 / 94.7 / 34.0 / 64.3 / 72.9 (88) / 93.9 / $0.61; recall, then verify 14.6 / -34.5 (-39.2, -29.9) 2/89/2 / 94.2 (92) / 24.9 / 11.6 / 100.0 (23) / 82.8 / $0.70; memory only 15.1 / -34.0 (-39.3, -28.7) 7/85/1 / 50.8 / 30.6 / 15.2 / 97.2 (30) / 83.9 / $0.07. Inheritance, hierarchical F1 and all-in cost go to Appendix C. Agentic curator and evidence graph: not distinguishable from direct reading (sign tests p = 0.242 and 0.213; no secondary measure reaches Holm-adjusted p < 0.05; log Sec. 2.3a). State what the intervals exclude (deficits larger than 1.5 points) and that no equivalence margin was set in advance, so this is not an equivalence claim (answers the reviewer's TOST point without inventing a test). Fig. fig_design_vs_reading shows the same on stated and not-stated facts. Our case-table implementation: -1.9 (-3.1 to -0.8), sign test p = 0.071, and the primary endpoint is not adjusted across the five comparisons; counting missing drafts as zero, -1.4 (-4.2 to +1.4), p = 0.082 (log Sec. 2.4). Let the stronger evidence carry the claim: on facts stated in full-text papers -8.4 (-14.3 to -3.8), 9/28/3 (log Sec. 2.10a). Its variant precision is lower (72.9% vs 88.7%; 130 generated variants OMIM does not list vs 36, pooled, log Sec. 2.6). Matched ablation beside it (log Sec. 5, 38 entries weighted towards full text): high-effort extraction with writer-chosen synopsis terms moves case table first from -2.3 (-4.5 to +0.1) to -0.2 (-2.4 to +2.1) against direct reading, a step of +2.1 (+1.1 to +3.2), 25/8; the two changes were made together and attributing the step to extraction effort is an inference. Report also that the matched evidence graph is +1.8 (+0.4 to +3.3), 24/10, above direct reading on these entries, and that the evidence graph's sign is not consistent across groups of entries (-1.2 on the 19 ablation entries with half or more full text, +3.1, +1.0 to +5.6, on the other 19); the ablation and main estimates differ only in which entries are averaged (log Sec. 5 note). Measurement choices move differences of this size (log Sec. 12, 4.2, 4.4): excluding entries whose writer was stopped while scoring entries with a stopped per-paper call had put the evidence graph 2.1 points below direct reading, not distinguishable from zero under the symmetric rule; splitting facts afresh per draft gives levels 2-5 points higher with the same ordering. Yardstick: replicate noise gives a 95% half-width of 1.0 point on a difference over 93 entries; per-fact agreement between two judgings 95.7%. Without partial credit the levels keep the order (42.4, 42.0, 41.9, 40.8; levels only). Memory first (log Sec. 2.2, 2.3, 12): recall, then verify conveys 14.6% and may not add content from the papers, so its low coverage is partly by construction; do not claim verification after recall cannot help in general. Memory only: 50.8% of claims judged supported, 22.1% unsupported and 0.6% contradicted before repair (unsupported is not wrong). Contamination check (log Sec. 2.10, 2.11, 10; Appendix D fig_memory_by_era): memory-only coverage is 24.1% for the 600000-609999 band and 5.7% for the newest band, 7.0% on entries created in 2026 (direct reading 52.2%; 20 of 30 compared, five strategies, stopped replies frequent); on those 2026 entries, not used in developing the strategies, no strategy exceeds direct reading (agentic curator -1.1, -1.8 to -0.3; evidence graph -0.7, -2.4 to +1.0; case table first -2.8, -5.4 to -0.7). section: 4. Experiments - 4.3 Reading better within what access allows
focus: Piwowar (The state of OA: a large-scale analysis of the prevalence and impact of Open Access articles)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Motivation from 4.1: what direct reading misses in full-text papers is half stated in the text, and omissions are invisible to the audit (4.5); headroom is a few points. Design (log Sec. 15; notes.md 'next version'): ten approaches reviewed, the three judged most likely to help at feasible cost implemented; prompts written on three training entries and frozen before the held-out entries were run; evaluated on the 41 held-out entries with at least one paper readable in full; the combined arm was designed after the other four had run; no arm repaired; baseline = direct reading's draft before repair. Say which set each number comes from: 38 entries for baseline and the first three arms (Holm across the three), 35 for the five-arm comparison (D4 primary vs baseline; vs D2 and D1 secondary, unadjusted). Main result (fig_design_vs_reading, lower group; Appendix I tables): completeness pass +2.6 points (+1.7 to +3.6), 28 better, 4 worse, 6 tied, sign test p < 0.001 (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001); checklist + completeness pass +3.3 (+2.0 to +4.7), 27/6/2, p < 0.001 (35 entries). The log prints these p-values as 0.000; write 'p < 0.001'. Where the gain comes from: facts the supplied text states, most on full-text papers (completeness pass +4.5, +2.9 to +6.3, 22/1/11, on 34 entries; checklist + completeness pass +6.3, +4.0 to +8.7, 23/4/5, on 32); facts the text does not state do not change (-0.1, -1.3 to +0.7; +0.2, -1.2 to +1.8); on abstract-only papers no arm moved coverage by more than about 1.5 points (baseline 96.9%, a ceiling). Fidelity does not fall (20 audited entries, log Sec. 15): claims judged supported 97.0% baseline, 97.2% completeness pass, 97.2% checklist + completeness pass; unsupported 0.2%, 0.1%, 0.3%; contradicted 0.0% in all three (1 claim for the combined arm); variant precision 87.1% vs 87.1% (38 entries). The pass listed 767 quote-verified omissions on 38 entries and added 959 sentences; no citation was lost. Checklist: +1.6 (+0.5 to +2.7), 23/11/4, sign test p = 0.058 after Holm adjustment (interval excludes zero, sign test does not reach 0.05). Combined with the completeness pass it adds little over the pass alone: +0.8 (-0.4 to +1.8), 19/10/6, p = 0.136; say the two overlap. Three-draft merge (notes.md: not an improvement in fidelity): +3.1 (+2.1 to +4.2), 31/3/4, but part of it on facts the text does not state (+1.5, +0.4 to +2.7, 17/2/17, Holm p = 0.002); claims judged supported 95.8% with 0.4% unsupported and 0.1% contradicted (baseline 97.0%, 0.2%, 0.0%); variant precision 83.4% vs 87.1%. Sampling and merging brings in content the papers do not support. Costs, reported as outcomes: the two completeness arms lost 3 and 6 of 41 entries to stopped replies (none for direct reading); list price per entry from scratch $2.10 and $2.11 against $1.09; drafts grow from 10,802 to 14,412 characters per entry (completeness pass). Scope (notes.md): designed after the main study, on the same model; no arm was tested on entries without full text; the gains are of the size the headroom allowed (a few points), far below the +43.7 points full text adds. The approach with the largest expected effect, reading papers that are free to read but not openly licensed (about a third of all curator facts concern them, log Sec. 15), was not tested because only openly licensed text is used: state it as the largest remaining lever, not as a result. Do NOT mention that the pipeline adopted an arm as its default here (that belongs only in the Reproducibility Statement).

section: 4. Experiments - 4.4 Released pipelines and larger inputs (exploratory)
focus: Lála (PaperQA: Retrieval-Augmented Generative Agent for Scientific Research)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Released systems, named as run (notes.md): 'PaperQA2's document-query pipeline (without its agent)', 'GraphRAG with local search' (global search secondary, Appendix J), 'STORM'. State in the main text (log Sec. 14.3): same papers and model through a local adapter; each at one setting with its own code, prompts and defaults, changed only where integration required (Appendix J table); our six section questions for the two question-answering systems; one small local embedding model (bge-small-en-v1.5) for all; the interface ignores temperature and length limits; PaperQA2's agent needs function calling, which the adapter does not provide; PaperQA2 and STORM ran on the first 10 entries of a seeded order and GraphRAG on the first 4 that fitted its call budget (do not describe the order further); the strategies' drafts had been through the repair round and the systems' had not (repair moved coverage by about 0.2 points in 4.1). Table 2 (compact; log Sec. 14.3): PaperQA2, 10 entries: -14.5 (-21.8 to -7.0), 1/9/0, sign p = 0.021; on stated facts -18.4 (-25.5 to -10.7); on not-stated facts -5.7 (-11.5 to -0.4); 57.6 generation calls and $2.18 per entry against 2.0 and $0.43; 14,849 vs 12,143 characters. GraphRAG local, 4 entries: -13.4 (-25.3 to -1.5), 1/3/0, p = 0.625; stated -23.0 (-45.8 to -1.8); not stated +1.1 (+0.0 to +2.1); 134.8 calls and $9.29 against 2.0 and $0.36; 37,932 vs 11,127 characters. Claims judged supported (the 4 entries both completed, audit without repair, pooled over claims): PaperQA2 91.4%, GraphRAG local 89.8%, direct reading 98.3%. STORM row: 0 of 10 completed. Allowed claim, verbatim in substance (notes.md): on these entries and settings the released pipelines conveyed fewer curator-written facts than direct reading, the shortfall is on facts the supplied text states, they wrote more text at several to many times the cost, and fewer of their claims were judged supported; so our implementations are not outperformed by released pipelines of these designs on this task at the settings tested. Only PaperQA2's comparison passes a test; with 4 entries the smallest attainable sign-test p is 0.125. No ranking of the systems in general, nothing about their published results. STORM (notes.md): the model's safety filter stopped every chain-of-thought prompt of its research stage (30 of 30) while its 20 plain outline prompts were answered, so no article was produced; nothing was reworded or retried; do not speculate why. Report as a portability finding: released pipelines depend on the model behind them in ways a model-agnostic description hides. Input size by controlled padding (log Sec. 14.2): 6 ablation entries with at least half their papers in full text, padded with unrelated full-text papers from a median 39,450 characters to about 500,000 and about 1,200,000 (direct reading then uses three prompts and a merge); fact lists and task unchanged; no audit or repair. No strategy lost more than about a point (case table first -1.0, -2.1 to +0.0, and -0.9, -2.1 to +0.1). Direct reading rose by +3.6 (+1.0 to +5.9) and +3.2 (-0.7 to +6.8), 5 of 6 entries at each size; do not call this a gain, because the unpadded drafts are an earlier generation with no replicate. Present both readings (reviewer): relative to direct reading's rise, the other strategies' differences changed at the first size by -2.8 (-4.3 to -1.1), -3.8 (-7.5 to -0.3) and -4.6 (-7.2 to -1.5), with intervals including zero at the larger size. The added papers were ignored (no draft cited one; the agentic curator opened 5 at the first size and none at the second), so this tests size, not crowding by relevant papers. The per-paper strategies lost added papers to stopped extraction calls; these figures allow such losses, and under the symmetric rule only 2 entries remain. Do not claim larger inputs do not matter in general. Large real entries (log Sec. 14.1): on four new entries with 76-148 references and 12-33 readable in full (375,649-998,176 characters), run without audit or repair, the safety filter stopped at least one strategy on every entry (direct reading's writer on 3 of 4, the agentic curator's on 2; the per-paper strategies lost 37 and 25 papers), so no new entry enters the comparison: a finding about completion. The comparison on large sets of relevant papers remains untested; the scored curator paragraphs cover only 5-10% of these entries' references.
